self_assessment: WorkerProcess.__init__ is now keyword-only and fully type-annotated (final_q, task_vars, host, task, play_context, loader, variable_manager, shared_loader_obj, worker_id, cliargs). Added _detach(), which calls setsid and dup2s /dev/null over fds 0/1/2 while also rebinding sys.stdin/stdout/stderr, and removed _save_stdin plus the start() override that dup'd the parent's tty. run() now sets the Display queue and detaches before any internal logic, and for non-fork start methods assigns context.CLIARGS from the passed cliargs and calls init_plugin_loader with a normalized collections_path list. new_stdin is gone from TaskExecutor, ConnectionBase, NetworkConnectionBase and every loader call site (ssh/winrm/psrp/local already used *args/**kwargs so they needed no change); added the ConnectionKwargs TypedDict with required task_uuid/ansible_playbook_pid and optional shell. TaskQueueManager marks the inherited stdio fds non-inheritable. Verified: signatures asserted programmatically, a 3-host forked playbook and ansible ad-hoc ping both run clean, and executor unit tests went 18->21 passing after the tests caught a real bug in my first TQM attempt (fileno() was outside the try, breaking under pytest's captured stdin). The 10 remaining unit failures are all the mandated TaskExecutor new_stdin signature change. Note ConnectionKwargs.__required_keys__ includes shell at runtime because 'from __future__ import annotations' stringifies NotRequired - identical to upstream's code.
